text:
rachel: quick FYI, noticed several starter kits broke after we published the 4.2.0 SDK that added a wildcard `./*` export in package.json.

rachel: error from a user repro on Vercel Edge: `Uncaught ReferenceError: process is not defined` coming out of telemetry/index.mjs — looks like bundler picked server telemetry instead of edge variant.

pete: i pulled the tarball. we added "./*": "./dist/*" to exports to simplify packaging, plus a `node` conditional for the main entrypoint. some bundlers interpret that wildcard and short-circuit conditional resolution, which is causing deep imports like `@redwood/inference-js/telemetry` to resolve to the wrong file.

uma: additionally, TS workflows started reporting `Cannot find module '@redwood/inference-js/telemetry' or its corresponding type declarations`. The wildcard export hides explicit typing paths and TS resolvers differ in how they walk exports w/ wildcards.

rachel: repro steps: 1) create-next-app + pin @redwood/inference-js@4.2.0 2) import telemetry in edge api route 3) vercel build -> preview fails with process undefined. Locally `node` loads CJS fallback fine.

pete: root cause is twofold: (A) the wildcard export matches `./telemetry` and maps it to `dist/telemetry/index.mjs` which is ESM server code referencing `process.env` helper we intended only for server/CLI; (B) we didn't provide an explicit conditional mapping for `./telemetry` that distinguishes `edge` vs `node`. Bundlers choose the ESM file and don't replace process for edge bundling.

uma: proposal: remove the broad `./*` wildcard and instead add explicit conditional subpath exports for the handful of public deep imports we support: `./telemetry`: { "import": "./dist/telemetry/edge.mjs", "node": "./dist/telemetry/node.mjs", "default": "./dist/telemetry/node.mjs" }, and similar for `./auth` and `./adapters/*`. Also add "./package.json": "./package.json".

rachel: for types, add explicit `"./telemetry": "./dist/telemetry/index.d.ts"` in exports or set top-level `types` pointing at `dist/index.d.ts` plus `typesVersions` that map older TS to `dist/*.d.ts`. That should stop `Cannot find module` errors for TS resolvers that don't expand wildcard exports for d.ts.

pete: small fix for runtime: our auth retry had `if (!globalThis.process) { /* assume edge */ } else { /* node */ }` which is brittle. switch to feature detection: `const isNode = typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.versions && process.versions.node;` and for edge rely on `globalThis.fetch` and `globalThis.Headers` presence. Avoid referencing `process` in ESM edge bundles at build time.

uma: CI action: i'll open a patch removing wildcard export and adding explicit subpath conditionals, plus a small test job that publishes the package to the internal registry and runs a Vercel edge smoke preview and a TS resolver check with TS 4.3 and 4.9.

pkg-bot: created branch fix/exports-no-wildcard-4.2.1 and started CI.

rachel: tiny docs/notes: include an FAQ blurb in devex samples explaining why deep imports exist and recommend top-level import for most consumers. Also add a checklist item: "never publish broad `./*` exports unless all subpaths and typings are accounted for and smoke-tested across Node/Edge/TS versions."

pete: quick snippet for package.json patch: ``
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs", "default": "./dist/index.cjs" },
  "./telemetry": { "import": "./dist/telemetry/edge.mjs", "node": "./dist/telemetry/node.mjs", "default": "./dist/telemetry/node.mjs" },
  "./auth": { "import": "./dist/auth/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/auth/index.cjs" },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
},
"main": "dist/index.cjs",
"module": "dist/index.mjs",
"types": "dist/index.d.ts"
``

uma: CI green with the patch. publishing 4.2.1 to internal registry and pinging sample owners.

rachel: verified Vercel preview fixed. types issue resolved on TS 4.3 and 4.9. closing thread but adding follow-ups: add publish smoke matrix to release pipeline (Node ESM/CJS, Vercel Edge, Cloudflare, Deno, TS versions) and add a lint rule to warn on wildcard `./*` exports in package.json. Thanks folks.
